quotes.text: An inbox rule lives inside one mailbox and runs after the message has already arrived. A mail flow rule lives at the level of the whole organization and runs before delivery.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates mail flow rules from inbox rules.

quotes.text: If you create a rule with no conditions and no exceptions at all, the action applies to every message in the organization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns about the most dangerous misconfiguration.

quotes.text: The order of your rules is itself a decision, and it deserves the same care as the conditions inside them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights that rule priority is a design decision.

quotes.text: Mail flow rules don't keep a history. There's no rewind button, and you can't roll a rule back to how it looked yesterday.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why admins must back up rules before changing them.

quotes.text: A good rule reads like a sentence you could say out loud, something like. When someone outside the company sends an invoice, add a warning. Unless the recipient is on the approved partner list.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a simple test for whether a rule is clearly defined.

chapters.title: What a mail flow rule is
Where it fits and beginner mistakes

takeaways: Mail flow rules run organization-wide in Exchange Online while a message is in transit, unlike Outlook inbox rules that run after delivery.
Every rule combines conditions, exceptions and actions, and rule order plus stop processing decide which rules actually act.
Rules have hard limits and no version history, so test them with policy tips, export a copy and write each rule down in plain language first.
hook: Every email in your organization passes rules that most users never see. This episode explains Exchange Online mail flow rules for admins and beginners, from conditions and rule order to limits and testing. You will learn how to build rules that add banners, signatures or encryption without blocking real mail.
